questions.question: If 21 tan θ = 20, then(1 + sin θ - cos θ) : (1 - sin θ + cos θ) is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

21 tan θ = 20

**Concept used:**

tanθ = P/B

sinθ = P/H

cosθ = B/H

P = perpendicular

B = base

H= hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

We know 20, 21 and, 29 is a Pythagorean triplets

So, 21 tan θ = 20

⇒ tanθ = 20/21

⇒ sinθ = 20/29

⇒ cosθ = 21/29

(1 + sin θ - cos θ) : (1 - sin θ + cos θ)

⇒ (1 + 20/29 - 21/29) : (1 - 20/29 + 21/29)

⇒ (29 + 20 - 21)/29 : (29 - 20 + 21)/29

⇒ 28 : 30

⇒ 14 : 15

**∴ Required value is 14 : 15**

questions.question: frac{{sqrt { cosec x - 1} }}{{sqrt { cosec x + 1} }} is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

√(cosecx – 1)/√(cosecx + 1) 

**Trigonometry identities used:**

sin²x + cos²x = 1

**Formula used:**

 a² – b² = (a + b) (a – b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ √(cosecx – 1)/√(cosecx + 1) 

(Here cosecx = 1/sinx

⇒ √[(1/sinx) – 1]/√[(1/sinx) + 1]

⇒ √(1 – sinx)/√(1 + sinx)

Rationalization

⇒ [√(1 – sinx)/√(1 + sinx)] × [√(1 – sinx)/√(1 – sinx)] 

⇒ √(1 – sinx)²/√(1 + sinx) (1 – sinx)

Here a² – b² = (a + b) (a – b)

⇒ (1 – sinx)/√(1 – sin²x)

Here 1 – sin²x = cos²x

⇒ (1 – sinx)/√cos²x

⇒ (1 – sinx)/cosx

⇒ (1/cosx) – (sinx/cosx)

Here 1/cosx = secx, sinx/cosx = tanx

⇒ secx – tanx ** 

∴ The required answer is __secx - tanx__**

questions.question: If P sin 60° = Q cosec 45°, then the value of (P²+Q²)/(P²-Q²) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the given equation: P/Q = cosec 45° ÷ sin 60° = √2 ÷ (√3/2) = 2√2/√3

Squaring both sides gives: P²/Q² = 8/3

Applying the Componendo and Dividendo rule directly:

(P² + Q²) / (P² − Q²) = (8 + 3) / (8 − 3) = 11/5

**∴ The correct answer is 11/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P sin 60° = Q cosec 45°

**Concept Used:**

Standard trigonometric values: sin 60° = √3/2 and cosec 45° = √2

**Calculations:**

⇒ P × (√3/2) = Q × √2

⇒ P/Q = √2 ÷ (√3/2)

⇒ P/Q = (2√2) / √3

Squaring both sides of the equation:

⇒ P²/Q² = (2√2)² / (√3)²

⇒ P²/Q² = 8/3

Let P² = 8k and Q² = 3k. Substituting these into the required expression:

⇒ (P² + Q²) / (P² − Q²)

⇒ (8k + 3k) / (8k − 3k)

⇒ 11k / 5k

⇒ 11/5

**∴ The correct answer is 11/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This property is highly useful for simplifying algebraic equations and expressions involving the sum and difference of terms.

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

It is essential to remember key angle values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, and sin 60° = √3/2. The cosecant function is the reciprocal of sine, meaning cosec θ = 1 / sin θ.

Basic Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ | 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

questions.question: The value of cot 13° cot 27° cot 60° cot 63° cot 77° is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If A + B = 90°, then cot A × cot B = 1.

Here, (13° + 77°) = 90° and (27° + 63°) = 90°.

So, cot 13° × cot 77° = 1 and cot 27° × cot 63° = 1.

Expression = 1 × 1 × cot 60° = 1/√3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/√3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cot 13° × cot 27° × cot 60° × cot 63° × cot 77°

**Formula Used:**

cot (90° − θ) = tan θ

tan θ × cot θ = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ cot 13° × cot 27° × cot 60° × cot (90° − 27°) × cot (90° − 13°)

⇒ cot 13° × cot 27° × cot 60° × tan 27° × tan 13°

⇒ (cot 13° × tan 13°) × (cot 27° × tan 27°) × cot 60°

⇒ 1 × 1 × (1/√3)

⇒ 1/√3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/√3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, sec(90° − θ) = csc θ, and tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

Reciprocal Identities

The product of reciprocal ratios is always 1: sin θ × csc θ = 1, cos θ × sec θ = 1, and tan θ × cot θ = 1.

Standard Trigonometric Values

Important values of cotangent are: cot 30° = √3, cot 45° = 1, and cot 60° = 1/√3.
</p

questions.question: What is the value of ((1+sec²A)/(1+cos²A)) ((1+sin²A)/(1+cosec²A))?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an angle, say A = 45°, to quickly evaluate the expression.

⇒ sec²45° = 2, cos²45° = 1/2, sin²45° = 1/2, cosec²45° = 2

⇒ Expression = [(1 + 2) ÷ (1 + 1/2)] × [(1 + 1/2) ÷ (1 + 2)]

⇒ Expression = (3 ÷ 3/2) × (3/2 ÷ 3) = 2 × 1/2 = 1

From the given options, tan²45° = (1)² = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is tan² A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = [(1 + sec²A) ÷ (1 + cos²A)] × [(1 + sin²A) ÷ (1 + cosec²A)]

**Formula Used:**

sec A = 1 / cos A, cosec A = 1 / sin A, tan A = sin A / cos A

**Calculations:**

⇒ First part = (1 + 1/cos²A) ÷ (1 + cos²A)

⇒ First part = [(cos²A + 1) / cos²A] ÷ (1 + cos²A) = 1 / cos²A

⇒ Second part = (1 + sin²A) ÷ (1 + 1/sin²A)

⇒ Second part = (1 + sin²A) ÷ [(sin²A + 1) / sin²A] = sin²A

⇒ Complete Expression = (1 / cos²A) × sin²A

⇒ Expression = sin²A / cos²A = tan²A

**∴ The correct answer is tan² A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Trigonometric Identities

Functions that are inverted forms of each other: sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ and cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ.

Quotient Identities

These identities relate tan and cot to sine and cosine: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ and cot θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

Value Putting Technique

In the simplification of trigonometric expressions, substituting an angle like θ = 45° easily converts complex variables into numerals, aiding rapid elimination of wrong options.
</p
